verdict.rationale: Jeeves documents its own API Platform. It has developer APIs for cards, payments, transactions and expense data, mTLS/OAuth 2.0 authentication, concrete endpoints such as POST /v1/cards/transactions and the Boleto lifecycle API, plus TypeScript/Python SDKs. However, the evidence shows only a few specific endpoints, the probes found no machine-readable OpenAPI spec, and the API is newly launched (December 2025), so how fully the product can be driven this way is unproven. Missing for 10: a retrievable OpenAPI/machine-readable spec, documented endpoint coverage across all product areas (accounts, FX, bill pay), evidence of open self-serve public access, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: API Platform: Developer APIs for cards, payments, transactions, and expense data. Launched December 2025.
The Jeeves API uses mTLS and OAuth 2.0 to authenticate requests.
Use POST /v1/cards/transactions with the source field to query card or travel transactions in a single endpoint.
The Boleto API supports the full boleto lifecycle, enabling clients to create, retrieve, extend, and cancel boletos via secure integration.
Batch payments, real-time webhooks, TypeScript and Python SDKs.
